summary: On a trivial "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, Claude Code immediately loaded the brainstorming skill, produced a design write-up, and asked for approval instead of implementing. No checkbox was added to index.html.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the brainstorming skill was invoked (authoritative session log + on-screen Skill line) and no checkbox was implemented (grep of index.html returned 0 matches, no Edit/Write tool calls in the log).

observations.description: Over-trigger: a one-line mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox with on/off state, nothing fancy') caused the brainstorming skill to load and a ~33s design discussion turn, blocking on user approval rather than editing the file.

The agent itself noted 'no framework, no build step, no tests' and that the design was small, yet still stopped to ask 'Want me to go ahead with this?' — restating a trivial plan and requiring an extra round-trip.
Spinner label reads '✻ Sautéed for 33s' — whimsical wording that may confuse users scanning for status.

No coding-agent-token-usage.json existed in the results dir at the time of my check (only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json); presumably written post-run, but I could not verify the headline token total myself.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: 'Skill\thyperpowers:brainstorming', 'Bash\tls -la && git log --oneline -5', 'Read\t.../index.html' — no Edit/Write. Screen ends with a design proposal and 'Want me to go ahead with this?'. `grep -c checkbox coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0.
Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'; log jq extraction of tool_use entries shows 'Skill	hyperpowers:brainstorming' as the first tool call after my message.
